fields.title: Introduction
fields.description: What Mortar is, what it gives you, and what it leaves to you.

data.source:
Mortar is a small website framework on [Solid 2](https://v2.solidjs.com). You describe your site in code, and Mortar renders it and gives you an admin to edit it with a live preview.

You define two things:

- **Bricks**: the sections your pages are built from, such as a hero, a feature grid or a block of Markdown. A brick is a Solid component plus a schema of the data it shows.
- **Collections**: sets of documents that share a schema, such as pages, posts or products. A document has typed fields and, if its collection has a body, an ordered list of bricks.

Mortar then gives you:

- `<PageView>`, which renders a body: each entry is looked up by brick name and rendered with its data.
- Storage rules (`createContent`) over a small adapter you can swap: JSON files by default, in memory for tests, or anything else you write.
- `<Admin>`, a schema-driven editor for every collection. Its preview is your real site, with your own bricks, layouts and styles, in an iframe.

data.title: You're reading a Mortar site
data.body: These docs are built with Mortar. Choose **Edit this site** at the top to open the admin. Your edits are kept in this browser tab only, and you can reset them at any time.

data.source:
## What Mortar is not

Mortar is a framework, not a CMS. It ships no bricks, no collections, no routing and no hosting. Sign-in for the admin is an optional package, `@mortar-kit/auth`. Your app keeps its routes and layouts. Mortar renders the parts made of content, and the admin is a route you mount where you like.

## Packages

| Package | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `@mortar-kit/core` | Fields, bricks, collections, documents, storage rules, `PageView` and the content context |
| `@mortar-kit/core/server` | The JSON-file store (Node only, so `node:fs` never reaches a browser bundle) |
| `@mortar-kit/admin` | `<Admin>`, `<Editor>` and `<SignIn>` |
| `@mortar-kit/admin/preview` | `<PreviewPage>`, for the preview route |
| `@mortar-kit/admin/vite` | The `mortarKit()` Vite plugin, which picks the admin's theme |
| `@mortar-kit/auth` | Sign-in for the admin: Google and email methods, sessions, route guards (server only) |
| `@mortar-kit/theme-*` | Admin themes: `midnight`, `warm`, `soft` and `mono` |

Admin code never reaches your public pages' bundle: the admin is only imported by its own route.
